Measurements should be organized in tables so you can compare items, analyze results, and spot patterns clearly.
Trade winds are steady winds blowing toward the equator, and when the northern and southern trade winds meet, they form the Intertropical Convergence Zone.
In the Intertropical Convergence Zone, warm air rises continuously, forming tall clouds that often bring heavy rain to places near the equator.
Aquatic ecosystems also have energy pyramids, with phytoplankton as producers at the bottom and larger fish as consumers at higher levels.

What happens to rocks in a reverse fault?

The rocks squeeze together, and one block slides up over the other! This can push the seafloor upward during a quake.

How do rocks move in a normal fault?

The rocks pull apart, and one block drops down! This can make the ground sink and change the shape of the land.
A simple fault model uses two blocks of wood with sandpaper between them! They slide past each other to show how rocks move.
